correctness.rationale: Cayley–Hamilton for 2x2 B=A^T A gives samplewise residual E(w)=det(B)||w||²/(w^TBw). A Gaussian direction is uniform on the circle, so integrating 1/(lambda cos² phi+mu sin² phi) yields 1/sqrt(lambda mu) and expected sigma1 sigma2. The four sign vectors reduce to two projective directions with Rayleigh quotients s±b; averaging gives D*s/(s²−b²). For fixed eigenvalues |b| ranges 0 to (lambda−mu)/2, proving the sharp harmonic/arithmetic squared-singular-value extrema and their basis equality cases. Solving E_R=E_G yields sin(2theta) cutoff sqrt(sigma1²+sigma2²)/(sigma1+sigma2). Uniform orientation measure gives the arccos fraction, its high-kappa expansion and orientation average. Independently tested direct projector/closed-form identities and numerical orientation cases; analytic proof covers all stated real A.

Under independent Rademacher entries it is det(B)*s/(s^2-b^2), varies sharply between det(B)/s and s, and admits an explicit orientation crossover and adverse-orientation fraction.
